1.name: Outer cylinder
1.note: The strut's body, bolted to the engine mount. Its upper part is the air chamber; the piston tube slides up into its bore.

2.name: Top fitting
2.note: Closes the top of the cylinder and hangs it from the engine mount on one big bolt. The orifice tube and the air valve screw into it.

3.name: Air filler valve
3.note: Where the strut is charged to 45 psi with the gear extended and unloaded. That charge sets how high the nose sits.

4.name: Gland nut
4.note: Screwed into the cylinder's lower end: the bearing the piston tube slides in, carrying its seal, an O-ring and the wiper.

5.name: Centering cam, fixed
5.spec: V notch fore and aft, 12 deep
5.note: Sits on the gland nut. When the strut extends fully after lift-off, the moving cam's teeth slide down its notches and turn the wheel straight.

6.name: Centering cam, moving
6.note: Pinned to the piston tube. Its teeth find the fixed cam's notches at full extension, so the wheel can't land or retract cocked.

7.name: Snubber ring
7.note: A one-way valve for the recoil oil: open while the strut compresses, shut while it extends, so the nose comes back up slowly and doesn't bounce.

8.name: Piston head
8.note: Screwed on the tube's top, it bears on the cylinder bore. Recoil oil passes its ports; the orifice tube passes through its middle.

9.name: Piston tube
9.note: The sliding lower half of the strut, full of oil. Pushing it in shrinks the air above, which is the spring that holds the nose up.

10.name: Lower plug
10.note: Closes the piston tube's lower end. The fork bolt passes through it, and the metering pin screws into its top.

11.name: Metering pin
11.note: Rises into the orifice as the strut compresses. The thicker it gets, the smaller the hole left for the oil, so the damping grows with the stroke.

12.name: Orifice tube
12.spec: Ø30 × 3, vent holes at the top
12.note: Hangs from the top fitting down into the piston tube and carries the orifice plate on its end. Oil forced up through it spills out of the vents.

13.name: Orifice plate
13.note: The damper: every millimetre of stroke pushes 1.55 cm³ of oil through its hole, and the faster it goes the harder it resists (force ∝ speed²).

14.name: O-rings and backup ring
14.note: Seal the air and oil in: on the piston tube at the gland, under the gland's thread, and round the top fitting's spigot.

15.name: Wiper ring
15.note: Scrapes grit and ice off the chromed tube as it slides in, so the seal behind it isn't cut.

16.name: Fork
16.spec: Crown boss, two legs, link lug
16.note: Straddles the wheel and carries the axle. It is bolted to the piston tube, so it rises and turns with it.

17.name: Fork bolt
17.note: Pins the fork's crown to the piston tube and its plug, fore and aft through all three.

18.name: Steering collar
18.note: Turns on the outside of the cylinder. The pedals pull its horns through the bungees; the torque links pass its turn down to the fork.

19.name: Torque link, upper
19.note: With the lower link it forms a scissors that lets the piston tube slide but not spin, so the collar can steer the fork.

20.name: Torque link, lower
20.note: Joins the knee to the fork's lug. The knee folds forward as the strut compresses and straightens as it extends.

21.name: Torque link bolt
21.note: The scissors' three pivots: collar to upper link, the knee, lower link to fork. Worn bolts here let the wheel shimmy.

22.name: Shimmy damper
22.spec: Ø28 hydraulic, pinned to the right horn
22.note: A small oil damper between the collar and a fixed bracket. Slow pedal steering passes; the fast wobble of a shimmying wheel is damped out.

23.name: Damper bracket
23.note: Holds the shimmy damper's body still against the cylinder, so the damper resists the collar turning.

24.name: Bungee spring cartridge
24.note: Spring links from the rudder pedals to the horns: they steer the wheel ±10°, but stretch instead of fighting the centering cams in flight.

25.name: Axle
25.note: A hollow axle clamped between the fork legs by a through-bolt; the spacer and sleeves set the bearings' places.

26.name: Wheel
26.note: Two halves bolted together through the web, so the tyre can be fitted without levering it over a rim.

27.name: Tapered roller bearing
27.note: One each side of the hub, facing apart, so together they take the wheel's weight and its side loads in turns.

28.name: Tyre and inner tube
28.note: The first spring: about 20 mm of squash under the nose load. The strut does the rest of the work, and the oil the damping.

29.name: Engine mount
29.note: The welded truss that carries the engine also carries the nose gear, so landing loads go into the firewall through it.

30.name: Strut clamp
30.note: The strut's lower attachment: a band round the cylinder bolted to the mount's lower leg, taking the drag and side loads.
